questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country i wanted to explore, and getting to know new people from all around the world.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Pretty easy.
However, i did find the entire process of finding a university, getting courses, filling out paperwork etc. was a bit commplicated.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: got assitance from haskoli university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student housing

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: i shared livingroom and kitchen with 8 other flatmates

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I can recommend it, the student housing is good

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to contact the host institution and get courses accepted, it was a bit complicated because the courses have different etcs points, which makes it hard to choose freely.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: i got help from both universities and other students

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: pretty succesfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you have to have 60% of courses of you own faculty! I did not get this in the beginning and had to find other cources which made the whole proces more delayed and complicated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Maybe they were a bit too easy to get good grades in, i mostly did not read any of the course material and it still went fine. This was however nice, since i had more time to explore the country and the culture

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: i loved the teaching style, more assignments, way more feedback, and more classes than in copenhagen university. I think there is much too learn from iceland.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The role and policymaking of international institutions 
Negotiations 
Introduction to security studies 
Applied gender studies for international students 
Qualitative research methods

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the role and policymaking of international institutions, introduction to security studies and applied gender studies for international students. i also think negotiations had a good prectical apporach.

questions.answer: I general the prices in iceland a really expensive

questions.answer: Alcohol and getting around was more expensive than i thought

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Museums, bars, cafes, gym, swimming pool with hot tubs and saunas, resturants

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: apllying for the gym, it is really cheap and great with a sauna. Plus going to the pool.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Make plans for going on trips to see the countryside, it can be expensive but it is and expirience of a lifetime

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Im from Denmark so getting adjusted to Iceland is very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: get over and say hi with a friendly attitude. it cannot go wrong, everybody is there because they want to get friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything just works great in Iceland. you find no problems.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
prepare for the applying in good time, it is complicated and takes a long time - and ask for help if you dont get it! 
Have an open mind, you cannot plan everything, but with an open mind you can be certain that good things will happen to you. 
Do it! You get an unforgetable expirience you will think back on for the rest of your life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know all these different people from around the world - very rewarding

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting it all prepared before a arrived. once i got here, it was all part of an amazing expirience

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
